ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a table, listing Sodium, Cadmium, Lanthanum by metal, with corresponding ions respectively Na⁺, Cd²⁺, La³⁺; their ionic radii are very close, respectively about 132 pm, 124 pm, 130 pm; the oxide melting points are respectively 1275°C (sublimes), 1500°C, 2256°C. Then reason: the problem asks to explain why the melting point of La₄O₃ is obviously higher than Na₄O and CdO. Since the radii of the three cations in the table are similar, ion size is not the main difference; the key difference is the charge number, the charge of La³⁺ is higher than Cd²⁺ and Na⁺. The lattice energy of ionic crystals increases as ion charge increases, therefore the electrostatic attraction between La³⁺ and oxide ions is the strongest, the lattice energy of La₄O₃ is the highest, so the melting point is the highest.
